title: An ultra-bright, highly-scalable, squeezed light source for hybrid quantum photonics
authors: Kai-Hong Luo, Denis Kopylov, Florian Lütkewitte, Jan-Lucas Eickmann, Simone Atzeni, Fabian Schlue, Benjamin Brecht, Torsten Meier, Polina Sharapova, Michael Stefszky, Christine Silberhorn
abstract: Hybrid quantum photonics seeks to combine the complementary advantages of continuous- and discrete-variable quantum optics. This typically entails photon-counting measurements on entangled states generated by interfering many single-mode squeezed-vacuum (SMSV) states. However, because conventional photon-counting schemes are mode-insensitive, it is critical that the SMSV states occupy a single, well-defined mode. Achieving this requires careful engineering of the process, which determines both the spatial and spectro-temporal properties of the generated state. In addition, the ideal source must be massively scalable, capable of efficiently generating strong squeezing, and remain compatible with existing detection schemes and fiber networks. Although many platforms address one or more of these requirements, satisfying all of them simultaneously remains challenging.   Here, we present a source that meets all of these requirements: a single-pass, periodically poled, Type-II potassium titanyl phosphate (KTP) waveguide optimized for scalable hybrid quantum-photonic architectures. The SMSV state produced by the source has a measured effective mode number of 1.24. Furthermore, the source is extremely bright (producing up to 40 000 photons per pulse) and operates at a central wavelength of 1546nm, optimized for fiber-network compatibility and which, in combination with picosecond duration, also enables intrinsic photon-number resolution in superconducting nanowire single-photon detectors. Although this source constitutes an ideal source in a simplified picture, the ultimate limitations of any source will be governed by complex dynamics that arise when the system is driven at high-gain or due to unavoidable loss during state generation. We have therefore developed a complete theoretical framework that enables a comprehensive photon-counting-based characterization of the source.
summary: This paper introduces a novel, highly scalable source based on a periodically poled KTP waveguide designed for hybrid quantum photonics. The source generates ultra-bright, single-mode squeezed vacuum states compatible with existing fiber networks and single-photon detectors. The authors complement the experimental results with a detailed theoretical model to accurately characterize the source's performance under realistic, lossy, and high-gain operating conditions.
main_problem: The challenge is to create a highly scalable, single-mode source of squeezed vacuum states necessary for hybrid quantum photonics, which combines continuous and discrete variable quantum optics.
main_result: The authors present a periodically poled KTP waveguide source that successfully meets all requirements: it is extremely bright, operates at a telecom wavelength (1546 nm), and generates near single-mode squeezed vacuum states.
method: The work combines experimental demonstration using a specialized KTP waveguide with a comprehensive theoretical framework to characterize the source, especially in the presence of losses and high gain.
model_or_system: The physical system is a single-pass, periodically poled, Type-II potassium titanyl phosphate (KTP) waveguide used for spontaneous parametric down-conversion (PDC). The theory models the source using the multimode spatial Langevin equation to account for complex dynamics, losses, and time-ordering effects.
key_observables: Effective mode number (measured as 1.24), brightness (up to 40,000 photons/pulse), squeezing level (approaching 20 dB), and the Joint Spectral Intensity (JSI).
important_parameters: Wavelength of 1546 nm (for fiber compatibility), picosecond pulse duration (for SNSPD compatibility), and high-gain operation regimes.
main_assumptions: The simplified single-mode theory is insufficient; the full theoretical framework must incorporate time-ordering and loss mechanisms for accurate characterization.
figures_summary: Not specified, but the notes indicate the comparison of theoretical predictions (using correlation matrices) against experimental measurements of spectral purity and photon statistics.
paper_structure: The paper first establishes the requirements for hybrid quantum photonics. It then details the proposed KTP waveguide source and its performance metrics. Finally, it develops and applies a rigorous theoretical framework to characterize the source's complex dynamics under high-gain and lossy conditions.
why_interesting: This work is highly relevant as it tackles the engineering challenge of creating robust, high-performance quantum light sources, which is foundational for building scalable quantum networks and quantum computation hardware.
